restaurants.name: Mall Bro

restaurants.name: Best Kebab
restaurants.notes: They visited this place and spoke with the founder who opened it in 1982. Jack described it as 'the best kebab of my life' - very delicious, clean, not greasy, with uniform minced meat. The founder recommended eating it simply with just onion, chili sauce, and lemon juice.
dishes: Doner kebab (100% lamb shoulder, kufta style)

restaurants.why: More Fallow personally visited and Jack gave a detailed, enthusiastic first-hand review of the food.

restaurants.name: Superb
restaurants.notes: Their final kebab stop visited around 1 am where they tried chicken doner, veal doner, and lamb doner. The chicken doner was described as comforting and well-made with high-quality ingredients, though not as luxurious as the lamb and veal options. Will and Jack discussed the quality and textures of each.
restaurants.verdict: High-quality ingredients; chicken good but lamb/veal more luxurious.
restaurants.why: More Fallow personally visited and tasted multiple kebab types, giving their own detailed comparative opinions.

title: Chefs Review One of London's Oldest Restaurants ft. Lagom Chef

restaurants.name: Pavyllon
restaurants.notes: More Fallow visited for breakfast and praised it as serving London's best eggs Benedict, croissants, full English breakfast, and French toast. Called it 'flawless' with no complaints.
restaurants.verdict: Flawless breakfast with the best eggs Benedict in London.
restaurants.why: More Fallow personally visited and gave their own positive opinion on the breakfast quality.

restaurants.name: Simpson's
restaurants.notes: Historic British restaurant opened in 1828, reopened by Jeremy King. More Fallow highly praised the food, particularly the roast beef which they called 'the best' and 'incredible', and noted the inspiring dining room atmosphere.
restaurants.verdict: Incredible roast beef at this historic 1828 institution.
restaurants.why: The candidate place 'Simpsons Tavern' at Cornhill is a different business from the Simpson's described as being on The Strand; the description suggests the Jeremy King-reopened fine dining restaurant rather than the Cornhill tavern.

restaurants.name: Nellie's Tavern
restaurants.notes: Invitation-only basement bar at Simpson's. More Fallow visited and had Negroni cocktails in this night bar before heading home.
restaurants.verdict: Invitation-only basement bar with excellent Negroni cocktails.
restaurants.why: Nellie's Tavern is described as a basement bar within Simpson's, not an independent venue; the candidate place 'Karellies' doesn't match and appears unrelated.

restaurants.name: The Ned
restaurants.notes: More Fallow attended a Michelin BBQ collaboration from Texas featuring Interstellar BBQ x La Barbecue. They tasted and reviewed multiple dishes including brisket, ribs, pork belly, mac and cheese, sausages, and a Texas lamb sandwich.
restaurants.verdict: Exceptional barbecue collaboration; remarkably tender meat and bold flavors.
restaurants.why: The candidate place 'Neds Bar' in Church Lane, NW9 is incorrect; The Ned is a historic luxury hotel and restaurant in the City of London, formerly Midland Bank, not a bar in northwest London.

title: Chefs Review the Best Ever Seafood Meal

restaurants.name: Dorian
restaurants.notes: Josh Niland's pop-up at Dorian. Will and Jack dined there and gave extensive, enthusiastic reviews of the entire meal, calling it one of the best seafood experiences they've had, with particular praise for the creativity, fish preparation, and dishes like the sea bass, blue mackerel, tuna Wellington, John Dory, and tuna cheeseburger.
restaurants.verdict: One of the best seafood meals ever tasted.

Sea bass rib with muscovado and soy glaze

restaurants.verdict: One of the best Indian restaurants in London
dishes: Marinated lamb ribs and veal chops

restaurants.name: Blacklock Shoreditch

restaurants.verdict: Incredible steakhouse with exceptional meat quality and service.
